text_fidelity_a:
Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer 2016 UPDATE: Every replacement tire for this trailer (12.5 inch tire) is total junk, except one: the [[ASIN:B00I3U8MSG Schwalbe HS158 Wheelchair Tire - Wire Bead (Grey - 12 1/2 x 2 1/4)]]. Trust me, I tried them all by now.
UPDATE:
After three years I decided to change the tires on this trailer. By luck I discovered that there exist 12.5 in scooter tires and pocket bike tires in widths of 2.5 and 2.75 inches. I opted for a pair of 2.75 knobby pocket bike tires in the hope that the added width would prevent some of tip overs I describe below. HUGE DIFFERENCE! I could still make this trailer tip with little difficulty but it is far more stable with the improved tires. So if you're considering this trailer be prepared to change the stock tires immediately (<$20x2 with free shipping if you shop carefully). You'll still want to run with low tire pressure but not nearly as low as with the stock tires. If you opt not to change the tires, read on so you know what to expect and read the comments, too.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
For what it is (the materials) this trailer seems over-priced. It sometimes tips over (often enough) traversing street and sidewalk surfaces via a handicap ramp and driveways (and vice versa). If and when it tips over the trailer doesn't take the bike (and you) with it, but if you are traversing from sidewalk to street, it tips in the middle of the intersection. Not good.

The trailer tires call for 35 PSI Max and if those tires are fully inflated with an empty load, this trailer will bounce all over creation at any larger imperfections in the riding surface and is at serious risk of tipping over.

The tilted, upward-leaning design approach (like a hand truck) is a good one because the footprint is small, it is easy to maneuver when un-hitched and one need not bend far over to access the trailer and its contents. The footprint is small enough so I sometimes take it on a transit bus without concern. But I believe the upward design, hitching to the seat post rather than the rear-wheel axle, as with most trailers, is the source of the stability problems.

The strapping system (2 are included) is just okay. You can do just as well or better with quality bungies. I bought some of the bags that Burley dedicates to this trailer but returned them. I now just cinch a plastic clothes hamper to the trailer with bungies and the hamper holds a ton.

A few things can be done to minimize the bouncing and tipping:

1. when unloaded, reduce the trailer tire pressure to 10 PSI or lower. The problem with this is if you go from empty to a moderate or full load in the same trip, you'll need to inflate the tires mid-trip, closer to max PSI to accommodate the additional load.

2. traverse driveways and handicap ramps completely perpendicular so that you don't catch a trailer tire on the ramp's raised shoulders.

3. slow down (a lot) in anticipation of any significant road imperfection for when 1 and 2 are difficult or impossible.

After close to two years I still use this trailer almost daily for shopping but I've learned to slow way down when traversing from sidewalk to street and keep my tire pressure to 10PSI or less when unloaded or with a light-to-moderate load to prevent tipping. Even with the PSI under 10, there are particular handicap ramps that I traverse frequently over which, if I don't slow down significantly, the trailer will tip over. Every time. No exaggeration.

I'm not completely sorry I own this trailer; it has a lot going for it: small footprint, carry-on size for air travel, etc, but I believe it needs some type of suspension to prevent tipping to make it a better value at $299.
text_fidelity_b: Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

Super Strong Braided Fishing Line - 4 Strands Multifilament Pe Fishing Line - Abrasion Resistant Braided Lines – Incredible Super Power line 10LB-133LB, 110 Yards-1100 Yards Good line for trolling or jigging. This is an economy version of the spectra superlines that allow you to hold more line and go deeper with less drag and almost no stretch. This line holds knots as well as any of the superbraids, and better than some of the coated, slicker lines.

This probably isn't the best choice for a casting reel. I'd look for an 8-strand line because its a little smoother and should pay out better than this 4-strand braid. The newer coated lines probably cast better, too. For trolling or jigging, though, this stuff works great, especially if you're on a tight budget.

Be sure to check the prices on all the different colors once you've selected the weight of line you want. Sometimes there's a deal on one of the colors that makes it really affordable. You might want to check the prices of larger spools of your selected weight, too. Sometimes you'll find that they've discounted one of the colors in a bulk-size spool that makes it cheaper than the smaller spools of the same weight test. Good luck on the water!

Let me know if my comments are helpful.

text_fidelity_a:
Eackrola 2/4-Person-Tent, Instant Pop up Tent for Camping, Easy Setup Beach Tent Sun Shelter - Ventilated Mesh Windows, Water Resistant, Carry Bag Included I got this tent to have a little pop up tent for the beach. I was assuming it was pretty small, easy to pack in the car and to the beach. But this tent is quite large. In its case it comes up to my waist or so (Iʻm 5ʻ7"). When opened up it easily fits my entire family inside. So itʻs a little large for my intended use, but I think it will be very useful when family camping.

Setting up this tent is the very definition of simple. I took it out of itʻs case and threw it on the ground. At first it took a while to open up, since all the windows and doors were shut and creating a vacuum in the tent. But once I cracked a window and air could get in it popped right open. The tent is quite spacious. I can lie down the short way and not touch the walls of the tent. If you are very tall, you probably would have to lie down the long way in the tent though. I canʻt stand up in the tent, itʻs about the height of your standard 4 man dome tent.

There are doors on either end, both with screens and rain flies. There are also windows on both sides. The windows have a zipper, so you can pass small objects through the window.

Breaking down this tent was challenging. It took me quite a while to figure it out. I watched the promotional video for this tent which briefly showed how to put away the tent. It was slightly helpful, but I was still confused. But now that I figured out how to do it, I can get it broken down pretty quickly, within 20-30 seconds at the most.

I think this tent will be great for a quick camping trip with the family when I donʻt want to lug around our huge cabin tent. Putting it up is simple, there is more than enough space for me, my wife, and two kids, and it is now pretty quick to break down. Even if we do bring the big tent, I think we will still use this tent. Either the kids can have their own tent or have it as a play area.
text_fidelity_b: Eackrola 2/4-Person-Tent, Instant Pop up Tent for Camping, Easy Setup Beach Tent Sun Shelter - Ventilated Mesh Windows, Water Resistant, Carry Bag Included

text_fidelity_a: ATN Shot Trak HD Action Gun Camera Best little on-gun camera I've bought so far.  I got the one without the laser and the one with the laser when it first came out.  The laser is good for short range or indoors, but pretty much a novelty outdoors, in my opinion and experience.  I've shot a lot of videos with this unit already this year, and they came out very well.  The audio is almost too good on my unit.  This microphone picks up almost every single creak and groan and breath and movement within a wide radius.  On several of my videos, it picked up deer walking thru leaves 20 yards away.  I really like how the operator just flips one lever, and then the red light comes on to let them know the unit is recording.  The mini SD card is a little tricky getting in and out, but what did you expect on a compact unit of this nature?  I use a wooden toothpick and gently push the card in to release the catch taking it out and put it in by hand as far as I can, and then I click the card into place with theh toothpick.  Battery life has been good so far, even in cold weather.  I love the fact that the recording magnification is fixed.  No more fumbling around with a zoom trying to get just the perfect magnification.  It is what it is, so just make sure it's recording (and don't forget to take the lens cap off like I did one time) and point and shoot.  It takes videos of deer-sized animals at 50 yards and under very well, and I also shot a nice buck this year with my muzzleloader at 116 yards, and it wasn't bad video at all.  Operator error is drastically reduced.  Also, if you have it indoors and take it outdoors, makes sure to wipe the lens with an scope lens cloth or similar if it fogs up on the outside of the lens.  Had that happen as well.  Again, operator error.  My unit has held up to 12ga 3" slug recoil from a bolt action shotgun, my 50cal muzzleloader, and a 175lb crossbow, and 70lb compound bow so far with no problems.  I paid about $88 on here, and $15 for the memory card (not included).  If you have a weapon that has a rail and you want to video, this is the one to get.  I imagine it would work great for paintball as well.  Buy it.
text_fidelity_b: ATN Shot Trak HD Action Gun Camera

text_fidelity_a: Real Relax Under Desk Treadmill, Portable, Slim Walking Pad Space Saving Motorized Treadmill for Home Office Workout, No Installation Required Okay, so I'm near the upper limit of the treadmill's rated weight support.  I got this as a way to get myself walking regularly.  Understand that I live in Texas and until this week when we had 24 hours of rain that resulted in 10 inches of rain - nearly as much as we were down for 3 months...before that we had I believe 67 days in a row of 100+ degree days with even the night temps barely dipping below 90.  Skinny people may be okay walking in that heat, but not a fat person trying to lose weight!  So, for me, I have been walking slow and in short "bursts" to get acclimated and able to move up in speed and time.  T had been wanting an easy treadmill to store as I live in a small house - a mobile home which is the early version of a tiny house, before tiny homes were a "thing."  Anyway, I have this in my bedroom stashed behind a chair next to my bed.  It is easy to pull out and step on to begin my walk.  At the moment, I am walking about 15 minutes at a time.  My goal is to get to 1 hour and then I can begin walking faster to get some cardio involved with the walk.  I have also incorporated yoga so that I am working on muscle strength as well.  This treadmill is helping, but I was afraid, when I got it, that it wouldn't work well for me because I was a bit too heavy for it.  That's why I would ask that the people who make this should look into making it sturdier for those of us who are trying to improve our heath by using a treadmill.  Make it handle 300 or maybe up to 350 pounds would make it helpful for those who want to take charge of their weight loss at home.

text_fidelity_a: HOTaitai Portable Butane Stove with Wind Guard and Carrying Case, Single Burner Gas Stove Sutiable for Camping Emergency Preparedness I got this (and a propane heater) for emergency blackout times.  The blizzard this year in Texas in February saw me in a house for five days with no heat, no electricity while keeping my kitchen and bathroom faucets on a running trickle so they didn't freeze.  I made it through those five days because I wore three layers of clothing, two pairs of socks, two hats and covered up with three blankets, plus I had water to drink, bread and peanut butter to eat...yep, I learned my lesson.  This burner will be an emergency way to heat water or food should the power ever go out like that again.  I have had this burner on outside and it works great.  Bought a 6-pack of the 1 pound propane canisters and just in case, I have a back up to this back up with the smaller, hiker's version that runs on the small sterno cans which I also got in a 6-pack.  The point is that this can be used in your yard as a side-by-side to your BBQ grill to heat up the chili to smother your grilled hot dog in or if you are sitting in your house, in the dark and need something hot in your belly - tea or tomato soup - this little burner can do the job.  I understand that you do have to be careful of the fumes, but I also have a carbon monoxide detector that I watch when using this item in the house.  This stove top is so easy to use - insert the propane canister, turn the knob to start and then adjust the flame to what you need and then turn it off when done.  When cool, remove the propane, put it back in the case and you're ready for it's next use.  Pricewise, I think it's fairly reasonable for summer camping and emergency use.
text_fidelity_b: HOTaitai Portable Butane Stove with Wind Guard and Carrying Case, Single Burner Gas Stove Sutiable for Camping Emergency Preparedness

Sportcraft Ladderball Ladderball was originally invented by cowboys to perfect their throwing ability. The idea was taken from South American cowboys who use the bolo for roping. Outdoor challenges like throwing balls and pitching horseshoes are always fun activities, so ladderball fits right in with these.

Any activity that gets everyone up and moving rates 5 stars with me! There's nothing worse than being a couch potato when you could be outside and burning off body fat. This outdoor game is literally for all ages. The set up is simply putting together plastic poles and corners, which is finished in 10 minutes. When you take it down, you remove the ladders from the bases and store it flat- a 1 minute task.

The base is secured to the ground with 4 curved pins. I found that adding more pins works better. They sell these curved pins for about $2.00 in a longer size in garden centers for securing ground covers, and they really work well, added to the pins provided. You could even make your own pins with old hangers, which are easy to curve and cut with wire cutters. The top side poles are numbered and have 4 black rubber bands included for keeping score by moving the bands on the poles. The 6 bolos come in 2 colors- red and blue. They are golf ball size and just as hard, so just make sure little ones and pets know not to get in the way of the thrower. The game is easy to play, each of the three rungs on the ladder are worth different points and the first player to reach 21 points wins.

I've played ladderball with other friends and this is actually one of the better sets made. Wood ones seem sturdy, but crack after a few hard throws, and most of the bases are not wide enough to take the throwing power and fall over, even with weight on the bases. For $24.00, this is a great set- just add some $2.00 curved garden center pins for solid stability and you're ready to get off the couch and have some great family fun and outdoor exercise!
text_fidelity_b: Sportcraft Ladderball

Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown

text_fidelity_a: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men I ordered this bike because the saddle on my used Walmart (I admit it) road bike was killing my nether regions.  I have been riding for a year now and despite the origin of my bike, I have fallen in love with the sport and I usually go out for 15-20 mile rides and just enjoy the freedom it provides.  However, this season, my saddle became so painful that the fun was turning into sort of torture-endurance.  I decided to look for a new saddle but I hear so many stories of people spending all kinds of money trying to find the "right" saddle and if my bike is any indication, I don't have hundreds of dollars to spend to go through different saddles.  Anyway, I read the reviews on this saddle and being a bigger guy (240 lbs), I decided to give it a whirl based on the cheap cost.  Now, keep in mind that I also ordered a pair Pearl iZumi Men's Quest Cycling Shorts that I had read about on Amazon.  I say that because I figured a seat AND shorts might help.  On my first ride out with the saddle and the shorts, I was able to ride for 30 miles with hardly any pain!  I did notice that there would be a little pain when the bike short padding would get bunched up but after a readjustment, I was fine again.  It makes me wonder if the seat would have caused pain without the shorts.  I highly recommend buying shorts if you don't own any!  I wish I hadn't waited so long.  The padding makes a big difference.  I did notice the stickers coming off after the first ride but I don't really care about that.  I would rather have a plain seat then one with logos anyway.  I was surprised at how soft the seat was.  Some people have said that it is still a firm seat but after riding on my previous torture device, I feel that this is almost too padded.  I do feel that this is a great seat.  For the price, I figured I could give it a shot.  I'm definitely happy with the purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men

However, the tube should have some relief cut length wise (4" or so) into the top end to assist in removing the rod. The rod has to be removed straight out the back without any angle but the pouch itself interferes to some degree. A 4" or so notch cut out at the top end would facilitate easy removal. The little storage pouches on the sides might be a nice touch for some but to me they were an unnecessary nuisance. Also, a nice dense closed cell foam fly patch would be nice.

CAUTION: I broke an Orivs 10 foot rod right off the bat putting it in this case. I use this type of case so that I can pull the rod down into two pieces, keep the reel on with the leader and fly so that all I have to do is put it together the next pull over or stream. That is the point of having the reel pouch. When I placed the rod into the case, apparently the tip went into one compartment and the butt into another. When I pushed the r\od all the way in the line came tight against the compartments and snapped the very tip of the rod....My bad, but just a word of caution. I now make certain that both sections of rod go into ONE compartment.

text_fidelity_a:
12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent Ok, you can decide if I'm either stupid or desperate. One of the biggest problems encountered working in my yard during the summer in Southwest Florida are these insanely aggressive deer flies. They bite hard,even through your shirt, but they seem to particularly like your cheek, neck or lips. They don't stop pestering you until they are either able to feed or you manage to kill them. The best method I have found so far is to patiently wait for one to land on you and then beat the crap out of it. The problem is that I encounter several of them every day.

So I fell for this flypaper on a hat deal, hoping against hope that it would work where other methods have failed. I have used it for four hours every day for five days in a row. The results: NOT ONE DEER FLY CAUGHT! They continue to buzz around me and I continue to impatiently wait for them to settle so that I can kill them, but not even one deer fly even managed to trap itself on the flypaper by accident.

The product headline says "Repellent Strips" but also discloses that it contains no chemicals or odors. If the product has no chemical on it, how does it repel the deer flies? The only way I can see this working is by attaching the strips to a tennis racket and swinging it at the incoming deer flies. At least I'd get some more exercise and maybe kill a few before they can bite me.
text_fidelity_b: 12 / Pk Deerfly Patches/TredNot Deer Fly Patch Odorless Repellent

text_fidelity_a:
POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel I am rating two stars because it does NOT perform as promised in an important area AND because the company never responded to my request for support.

First, I'm an experienced swimmer; I'm 60+ but I can still swim a mile in under 30 mins and complete a 200 IM, so it's not like I don't know what I'm doing in the water. I've tried and tried -- and really tried -- to love this.

Pluses: SWIMMING with the Powerbreather is a breeze, and I actually enjoy the stress it places on my lungs, forcing me to breathe deeply. When I am swimming point to point I can work on my stroke, don't have to gasp to breathe, etc.

Negative: But doing flip turns is a nightmare! No matter what configuration I try, when I flip the tube fills w/ water and, because it is LITERALLY screwed onto the head, I have to race to release it before I am breathing water. Choking, gasping... this is not my idea of a good time. I've re-read all the literature, and everything points to my being able to do flip turns, which is specifically why I purchase the most expensive version, the Wave. I've reviewed all their pictures and videos, and notice that NOWHERE do they demonstrate anyone doing a flip turn using the device. Interesting. I've written to their customer service on their website asking for help and complaining I can't complete a flip turn w/o taking on water and is there any help they can offer and... crickets. Nothing.

I even had a swimming buddy try out the unit, thinking that "maybe it's me... maybe my flip turns are off." Nope, he took on water, as well.

I am keeping this because I do enjoy open water and ocean swimming, and occasionally it's useful to work on my stroke in the pool, as long as I'm OK doing clumsy top-of-water turns at either end of the pool. But I am terribly disappointed I cannot actually work out in a pool using the breather.
text_fidelity_b: POWERBREATHER Wave Snorkel

MOON LENCE 2 PCS Body Boards for Beach Lightweight with EPS Core & Wrist Leash 33/37/41" Body Board with Slick Bottom Surfing for Kids Teens and Adults My wife and I love going to the beach and had been wanting body boards for a long time. So when I had the chance, I grabbed these MOON LENCE Body Board - we are thrilled with them! Ok, maybe we’re just big kids at heart, but that’s the way life should be, so riding the waves is a lot of fun and today we spent a couple hours on these boards. From start to finish it was a great time and we can’t wait to go back... except, we are pretty sure this was the last weekend it’ll be warm enough even in our hot weather state, so yea, we wish we’d gotten them earlier, but no worry, we’ll have them for next year (or next weekend with any luck).

They are a great set - two is always better than one when you’ve got two people as you don’t have to share. We went with the yellow because let’s face it, they’re easy to see - they really are! The materials are excellent. The front has a slight texture that feels good - meaning you’re not scratched or feel rough when laying on it - and it lets you have a better grip. We had decent waves today and never once felt like we didn’t not have control. The back is smooth and rides the wave well. It is so well designed and done - compared to others we have looked at and not bought - that we would most certainly look at more in the future from the same line. I”m a bit heavier at present and I was still able to get the waves - though we could not get out as far and I was dropping deeper than my wife so had to watch in the shallower waters. The strap for your wrist was great. My wife put them on - they come unattached - and did mention it’s threading the needle - needs a soft touch, yet easy to do. Once on they STAYED ON! I mean you’d have thought these were pro boards or something they felt, looked, and rode so well. It was a bit of an effort getting the velcro undone the first time - we both ended up pulling from the inside to get it open - but in the end, they stayed secured to us as the waves let us have it. We had a great time today - and as mentioned above, hope we get maybe another weekend out there. Thrilled to have these MOON LENCE Body Boards!

text_fidelity_a:
NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako Got this to mount a MiNewt 150 on my helmet, and it's working well so far. It's kind of a tie-down thing with some pipe-insulation-like rubber under the plastic foot/pedestal to keep it from sliding around on the helmet. I've had it for about 2-3 weeks, so I can't comment on durability, but it has the same quick-release setup as the handlebar mount packaged with the 150. It tilts front and back, though not side-to-side. I'm using it with a Bell road helmet, and had no problems mounting it right in the center--as long as you have symmetrical vents in your helmet, you should be ok.

Good Stuff
With the right adjustments, you can get a good view of what's (well) ahead of you, and having it helmet-mounted allows you to pan and sweep the road ahead for pointy stuff and potholes. I also use it to alert drivers when approaching intersections--a quick look left and right gives a flash in their direction to get attention. The on-helmet setup seems to allow for longer "reach" from the light as well. One added bonus--drivers of high-profile vehicles (monster trucks, etc.) are more likely to see you since the light is well above the handlebars.

Notes and Concerns
If going for long rides in the dark, I'd recommend keeping a small blinky on the handlebars to complement the helmet mount (if you're not looking straight-ahead, your light isn't either). The mount is also made mainly of plastic--not sure what that does for long-term durability--may want to take it off if not doing night/dark rides, to minimize UV damage in the sun, etc. The mount does make the light sit rather high on the head, so it's not going to improve your aerodynamics or get you any style points (like a Roman centurion helmet profile), and it of course adds a bit of weight to the helmet.

Overall
I'd recommend this, especially for anyone who rides in the dark frequently or for long periods of time.
text_fidelity_b: NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz I simply LOVE my insulated Eddy Cambelbak bottle!
I didn't have a clue what they were all about, nor how a bite valve worked, but I needed a water bottle and started reading up about them. I am converted!
This bottle is very well constructed, and although tall, it doesn't take up much space on a desk or side table, and it holds a good 0.6L volume of lovely iced water.....and it doesn't "sweat"! Fantastic!
It keeps my water nice and cool for ages, and it is so convenient that I find myself drinking a lot more water that before, which is a good thing.

For anyone else that doesn't know what bite valve is (can I be the only one??!) - the "spout" of this bottle is made of a firm silicon rubber and it has a closed hole that attaches down to the bottle's straw. When you bite the end of this spout or valve, it squeezes the hole open and you just suck up the water like drinking from a straw. The second you take pressure off and stop biting down, the hole closes shut again and - voila! - A leak proof bottle! It is a fantastic design - I love it! (see pic)

The valve part can be in an angled or upright position, so you don't have to tip the bottle sideways to get the water to flow, and it also pushes right back to a "closed" and flat position which is great if you have it in a backpack, beach bag etc. It is just a really innovative design and it really works so well!!
I highly recommend this bottle to anyone who wants a fantastic, no sweat, leak-proof, easy to use drinking bottle - 10/10 !
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz

Auoxer Fitness Exercise Weighted Hoola Hoop, Detachable and Size Adjustable Design, Lose Weight Fast by Fun Way, Fat Burning Healthy Model Sports Life This Auoxer hula hoop comes with no instructions or suggestions. The picture on the box is the only hint as to its assembly however, it is fairly intuitive. The difficulty is joining segments 5 and 6 if you want the smallest opening size. It requires some muscle to force the ends to line up. I sat in bed and pushed the opposite (assembled) end against the top of my foot to force it into a somewhat round shape so I could join 5 to 6. The more segments used the easier it is to assemble.

Disassembly is more difficult and don't do it after a fresh manicure - it can be a nail breaker. You have to roll back about an inch of the foam covering and find the orange button, depress it hard, then continue depressing as you pull the segments apart. This alone will burn a few calories. Personally, I'll only be using it at home so I won't be disassembling it.

The opening size by number of segments:
6 segment opening size: 26”
7 segment opening size: 31”
8 segment opening size: 35”

There is a mild chemical-like plastic smell, but after 2 days out in the garage it went away.

I suppose if the assembly/disassembly were easier the hula hoop might not hold up to repeated use, so I forgive that difficulty. I do like that it's adjustable and the foam covering is a nice touch. Now if only I could remember how I hula hooped as a kid. I used to have simultaneous hoops on both arms and my waist while moving around. Now I have to concentrate to keep this one hoop from falling to the ground! That's ok, it will come back to me and in the meantime I have some hearty laughs each morning.
text_fidelity_b: Auoxer Fitness Exercise Weighted Hoola Hoop, Detachable and Size Adjustable Design, Lose Weight Fast by Fun Way, Fat Burning Healthy Model Sports Life

I'd say it's warm enough for three-season camping in most temperate zones, though you'd probably want to be wearing warm clothes or jammies, too, in a cool spring or late fall. ESEE Lite Machete Micarta Handles and Sheath This is by far the best machete I have owned and used during my 33 years living in Southwest Florida. I am a big knife collector and ran across this machete by chance when researching other big knives. Previously I had used several Cold Steel machetes which were quite satisfactory--until I discovered and started using the Esee Lite Machete.

Yes, the price point is higher, but what you get is a long, well-balanced, razor sharp, light weight, and flexible blade that cuts through 3" to 5" limbs like the proverbial "knife through butter". Besides that, all Esee products are guaranteed for life. While I haven't abused one to the breaking point yet--although I've tried--all you have to do is send it back to the company for repair or replacement (at the option of the company).

I take two of them into the wetlands with me when cutting Brazilian Pepper trees. Sharpening them is simple with the proper stone and they hold their edge far longer than lesser machetes made of softer steel. You can use them for hours with minimal fatigue because of the good grip, fine balance and light weight. The only better knife that I can compare it to is my Busse Nuclear Fusion Battle Mistress which costs upwards of $500.00. However, the NFBM is considerably heavier and has a thicker blade. This causes shallower cuts and quicker arm fatigue.

So ante up a few extra bucks and enjoy the superior cutting power of the Esee Machete. You will never buy another cheap machete because you will be spoiled by your new Esee.

NOTE 02/15/15: I finally found a drawback to the Esee Lite. The areas I work in are so thick that if you drop the machete or put it down and forget where you put it, it's almost impossible to find. So now I spray the handle with fluorescent orange paint which makes it much easier to see and recover.
text_fidelity_b: ESEE Lite Machete Micarta Handles and Sheath

Always remember to use extreme caution when handling knives. An old-timer once told me that they are just as dangerous as guns because they are always loaded. One slip can have disastrous results. Rollerblade RB 80 Unisex Adult Fitness Inline Skate, Black and Yellow, Urban Performance Inline Skates The sizing recommendations say to purchase this skate 0.5 to 1 size larger than our shoe size, but when I did that the front of the skate was way too loose (big). The problem with the current generation of Rollerblade skates appears to be that they are making the plastic shells harder which makes them harder on our ankles and harder to adjust the front of the skates.

If you choose to still purchase a Rollerblade hard-shell skate (Twister...), be very careful about understanding the return policy. Amazon.com apparently does not accept back rollerblade skates that have at all been skated outside. If you purchase Rollerblades, do not skate with them outside your living room without first being 100% confident that you have purchased the right size because you likely will not be able to return them. There are third party stores that provide much better return policies for inline skates (new or used-once), and so google until you find a skate and a store that gives you peace of mind.

I have a 10.5 shoe size, and I tried the 2018 rollerblade hardshell skates in 10.5, 11, and 11.5, and they all had the same ankle position issue. The issue is that my ankle is always close to the shell edge where the laces are, and so this generation of rollerblade skates all cause ankle pain. The workaround is that I took my skates to an ice skating pro shop where they used a heat gun to adjust the skates (it took 3 trips and a pretty significant adjustment). When the 2019 skates arrive, I will again check the 11.5 skates to see if they have the same issue.
